- When sentiment is negative (avg < 0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 30d mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high.
- If sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending upward, model may overfit upward momentum; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% per negative sentiment unit.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in early 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast mean.
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and apply 0.5–1.0% upward bias.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model tends to ignore it; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast mean.
